commands.command:
set -eu
printf 'os='; . /etc/os-release; printf '%s\n' "$PRETTY_NAME"
printf 'boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf '%s\n' '--- active pwquality-related lines ---'
for f in /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  printf '[%s]\n' "$f"
  sed -n '/^[[:space:]]*#/d; /^[[:space:]]*$/d; /minlen\|minclass\|[dul]credit\|ocredit/p' "$f"
done
printf '%s\n' '--- PAM references ---'
grep -Rns 'pam_pwquality' /etc/pam.d/system-auth /etc/pam.d/password-auth 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s\n' '--- authselect ---'
authselect current 2>&1 || true

--- pwquality drop-in documentation ---
       /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf

DESCRIPTION
       pwquality.conf provides a way to configure the default password quality
       requirements for the system passwords. This file is read by the
       libpwquality library and utilities that use this library for checking
       and generating passwords.

       The file has a very simple name = value format with possible comments
       /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d directory in ASCII sorted order. The
       values of the same settings are overridden in the order the files are
       parsed.

OPTIONS
       The possible options in the file are:

       difok
	   Number  of  characters in the new password that must not be present

commands.command:
set -eu
policy=/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/99-infraset-password-policy.conf
install -o root -g root -m 0644 /dev/null "$policy"
printf '%s\n' '# Managed password complexity policy' 'minlen = 12' 'minclass = 3' > "$policy"
restorecon "$policy"
printf '[%s]\n' "$policy"
stat -c 'mode=%a owner=%U group=%G selinux=%C' "$policy"
cat "$policy"
commands.stdout:

# Managed password complexity policy

minclass = 3

commands.command:
set -u
check() {
  label=$1
  candidate=$2
  output=$(printf '%s\n' "$candidate" | LC_ALL=C pwscore 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  printf '%s rc=%s output=%s\n' "$label" "$rc" "$output"
}

check long_16_two_classes 'abcdefghijklm123'
